T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Broader "bring your own power" datacenter trend, 300MW fuel cell buildout, AI datacenter energy demand growth

Synopsis:
DataOne's AI datacenter in Vineland, NJ — tied to a $17bn Nebius/Microsoft deal — is operating 45+ unpermitted diesel generators near schools and residential areas, in apparent violation of federal and state air permitting law. NJDEP has issued no permits and is moving toward enforcement. The facility, intended to be powered by 300MW Bloom fuel cells, is relying on generators as a stopgap. The case exemplifies the "bring your own power" trend across US AI datacenters, where speed-to-market is prioritised over regulatory compliance. Noise complaints, stop-work orders, and a class-action lawsuit are escalating pressure.

---

The article is US-focused, but carries implicit relevance: Nebius is a Dutch AI infrastructure firm, and the broader AI datacenter energy demand surge (including the "bring your own power" gas trend) is a structural driver of global gas demand, with direct read-across to TTF gas pricing. AI power demand narratives increasingly influence EU energy market sentiment.

**Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?**

The general theme — AI datacenters straining power grids, regulatory non-compliance, "bring your own power" gas strategies — is widely known and already priced into market narratives. This article adds granular detail on one specific facility but does not introduce a structurally new risk vector.
